fix_commit.message: Add the SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag to sqlite3_prepare_v3(). Use this to prevent fts3/4 tables in non-trusted schemas from calling unsafe SQL functions.
fix_commit.author: dan

findings.title: FTS3/4 internal SQL statements bypass trusted-schema protection against unsafe SQL functions
findings.message: Commit 4b136ed70a marks the FTS3 virtual table as SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS (ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3DeclareVtab), lowering its eVtabRisk to zero so that FTS3/4 tables can be created and used even when PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF (i.e. from untrusted/attacker-influenced schemas, such as those found in an attached or shared database). Before this change, SQLite's virtual-table risk checks (vtabIsReadOnly in src/delete.c, selectExpander in src/select.c) would block any access to FTS3/4 tables coming from an untrusted schema, so the module's internal SQL plumbing was never reachable in that threat model. After marking FTS3/4 innocuous, that protective gate disappears, but the module's internal SQL statements -- generated with sqlite3_mprintf() from schema-controlled strings (p->zName, p->zDb, p->zReadExprlist, p->zWriteExprlist, etc. -- see fts3SqlStmt in ext/fts3/fts3_write.c, fts3CursorSeekStmt/fts3FilterMethod in ext/fts3/fts3.c, fts3DoRebuild and sqlite3Fts3IntegrityCheck in ext/fts3/fts3_write.c) -- are still compiled via plain sqlite3_prepare_v2()/sqlite3_prepare_v3() calls with no indication that they originate from (and embed data governed by) a database schema. Because these statements are prepared as brand-new top-level Parse contexts, pParse->pToplevel is NULL and no Expr carries the EP_FromDDL/fromDDL flag, so the engine's existing 'disallow unsafe/DIRECTONLY SQL functions reached from untrusted schema content' checks in sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable (src/expr.c), vtabIsReadOnly (src/delete.c) and selectExpander (src/select.c) never trigger for them. The net effect is that an FTS3/4 virtual table defined inside a non-trusted schema can smuggle a call to an application-defined 'unsafe' SQL function into the engine, because the internal statements FTS3/4 prepares on its own behalf are never marked as DDL-derived and therefore are not subjected to the trusted-schema restriction, defeating the purpose of PRAGMA trusted_schema=OFF / SQLITE_DBCONFIG_TRUSTED_SCHEMA.
findings.suggestion: Whenever a virtual table module (FTS3/4, FTS5, RTREE, or any other module marked SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS) prepares SQL statements on its own behalf using text assembled from schema-controlled identifiers, those statements must be prepared with a flag that marks them as schema/DDL-derived so the existing trusted-schema enforcement (sqlite3ExprFunctionUsable, vtabIsReadOnly, selectExpander) still applies to them. Concretely: add an SQLITE_PREPARE_FROM_DDL flag to sqlite3_prepare_v3(), thread it through Parse->prepFlags, and OR it into the trusted-schema checks (pParse->pToplevel!=0 in delete.c, pFrom->fg.fromDDL in select.c, ExprHasProperty(pExpr,EP_FromDDL) in expr.c) alongside the existing conditions; then update every internal fts3/fts3_write prepare call to go through a wrapper (e.g. sqlite3Fts3PrepareStmt) that always sets this flag.

ground_truth.root_cause: SQLite's 'disallow unsafe SQL functions from untrasted schema content' protection was implemented by checking whether the current parse was a nested sub-parse of a top-level statement, or whether a specific expression was parsed directly from schema/DDL text. It did not account for virtual-table modules that, having been granted SQLITE_VTAB_INNOCUOUS status (and thus made usable from untrusted schemas), independently compile their own fresh top-level SQL statements built from schema-derived strings. Those internally-generated statements were indistinguishable, from the enforcement code's point of view, from ordinary trusted top-level user SQL, so the protection silently did not apply to them.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: FTS3/4 internal SQL statements bypass trusted-schema protection against unsafe SQL functions
